+++
title = "WebAssembly + WebGPU Integration Test"
date = 2026-01-06
description = "Example WebAssembly + WebGPU simulation."
+++

Example WebAssembly + WebGPU simulation.

<div style="width: 100%; height: 400px; border: 1px solid #333; background: #000;">
    <canvas id="bevy-canvas" oncontextmenu="return false;"></canvas>
</div>

<script type="module">
    // Import the init function from the file generated by wasm-bindgen
    import init from '/wasm/spinning_cube.js';

    function showFailure(reason) {
        console.error("WebGPU simulation unavailable:", reason);
        const canvas = document.getElementById("bevy-canvas");
        if (canvas) {
            canvas.style.border = "2px solid red";
            canvas.style.background = "red";
        }
    }

    async function run() {
        // Bevy's wgpu backend commits to WebGPU whenever `navigator.gpu` is
        // merely present, then panics deep in an async render task if no
        // adapter is actually available — a panic that happens after init()
        // has already resolved, so it can't be caught below. Check for a
        // working adapter first so an unsupported browser fails visibly here
        // instead of an uncaught panic in the console.
        if (!navigator.gpu) {
            showFailure("navigator.gpu is not available in this browser.");
            return;
        }

        let adapter;
        try {
            adapter = await navigator.gpu.requestAdapter();
        } catch (e) {
            showFailure(e);
            return;
        }
        if (!adapter) {
            showFailure("No WebGPU adapter available (no compatible GPU/driver found).");
            return;
        }

        try {
            console.log("Loading WASM simulation...");
            await init();
            console.log("WASM initialized successfully.");
        } catch (e) {
            showFailure(e);
        }
    }

    run();
</script>
